author: clean-loop7 SME critic (independent Claude critic subagent, 2026-11-19)

findings.claim: The residual the test does not detect is now described more narrowly than it really is. At 0aa7c2d1 the solved-run record's variantRuns (line 49) gives what reads as the full list: 'Not covered and not detected by the test: paused, long-delayed, very long, slow or endless animations that change a width or padding, and animated custom properties'. At 4cc61c8e the same list covered 'paused, long-delayed, very long or slow animations and animated custom properties that change the drawn size later', with no restriction to width or padding. The lab.json notes at 80eff5af (line 87) changed the same way, to '(for example a paused, delayed, very long or endless one that changes a width or padding)'. That text says 'for example', and the width-or-padding clause can be read as applying only to 'endless', so lab.json is ambiguous and incomplete rather than false. Read together, both now suggest that transform-type and zoom animations are detected. Four kinds are not. In each case below I ran a fresh git archive of 80eff5af with the private completed work plus one added rule, through the full suite. Each passed all 12 tests in every run. The same unmodified page, opened in the pinned Chromium at 1280x1000 with no test handling, draws the day tag at a width other than 200px (checked by getBoundingClientRect, and for the zoom case also by Playwright boundingBox and element-screenshot pixel width). (1) The owner-accepted cl5 residuals, now mis-described by the narrowed list. These were a paused finite animation, a 100000s animation, and a 100000s-delayed animation with backwards fill. Each holds a reduced scale on both tags or a reduced zoom on the checklist and ends at identity. Each passed 3 of 3 runs. finish() jumps them to their identity end values, which the identity rule then accepts. The page is drawn wrong at all six samples from 0.3s to 3.1s. (2) An endless transform or individual-scale animation on the tags whose keyframes rest at the literal value none for part of each cycle. It passed 5 of 5 runs and is drawn wrong at 2 of 6 samples. Between two none keyframes the computed value is the keyword none, which the strict branch (line 157) accepts. By contrast, a pulse interpolated from none or from 1 computes to scale 1 or an identity matrix and is rejected 4 of 4. (3) An endless zoom pulse on .site-aside starting at zoom 1. It passed 5 of 5 runs and is drawn wrong at 4 of 6 samples. Computed zoom has no none keyword and its initial value is 1, so the strict branch's String(cs.zoom) === '1' cannot tell a running zoom animation at that moment from the resting value. The same zoom pulse on the tags also passes 4 of 4, but this Chromium draws those tags at 200px, so I do not count it. (4) An endless scale pulse from 1 on .page, an element around the checklist. It passed 5 of 5 runs and is drawn wrong at every sample. Only the checklist's and the tags' own animations are inspected, and the rendered-width check sees scale 1 at the moment of reading. Cases (2) and (3) also pass all 12 with the loop-5 test file from ea630d09 (3 of 3 each), and case (4) follows from code unchanged since then, so none of the four is a loop-7 regression in behaviour. The regression is in the description, which loop 7 narrowed. Medium rests on cases (2) to (4). They are wrong pages that pass in every run, and no residual list names them. That goes beyond a wording slip, though it is bounded: it needs a deliberate keyframes rule, the calculated width is still measured, and README task 11 Outcome (line 141) and README line 17 forbid all four in general terms, so a learner who follows the README is not misled. It matters for maintainers and for the pending owner decision on cl6-sme-001, which should be taken on the real scope of what the test does not detect, not on 'width or padding'.

evidence.section: 4. The zoom property (property table: Value <number [0,inf]> | <percentage [0,inf]>; Initial: 1; Computed value: as specified, with percentage converted to number; no none keyword)

5 Individual Transform Properties: the translate, scale and rotate properties (scale property table: Value none | [<number> | <percentage>]{1,3}; Initial: none; Computed value: the keyword none, or a list of 3 numbers)

4.4.13 Finishing an animation (the procedure silently sets the current time to the associated effect end and resolves the start time, cancelling a pending pause, so a paused, very long or long-delayed finite animation is measured at its end values)

findings.recommendation: No new detection mechanism is needed for this finding. Reword the record's 'not covered' list and the lab.json residual so they match the test. For example: 'It does not detect animations whose state at the moment of measuring looks right but that change the drawn size at other times. These include paused, long-delayed or very long animations of any size, box, transform-type or zoom property, which finish() jumps to their end values. They also include endless animations of a width, a padding or zoom, endless transform-type animations whose value at that moment is exactly none, animations on elements around the checklist, and animated custom properties.' Give the owner's cl6-sme-001 decision the same scope. Optionally list in the record a none-resting endless pulse, an endless checklist zoom pulse and an endless .page pulse as known undetected variants, so later critics do not report them as new.

items.note: Loop-6 part closed. unscaledNow (lines 155-167) applies the strict none/'1' comparison whenever any animation on the element is not finished after the finite ones are finished, on the tags and on the checklist. On a fresh git archive of 80eff5af with the private completed work plus one rule each, full suite, each of these failed task 11, and only task 11, in every run (5 of 5 unless noted): an endless alternating scale pulse from 1 on both tags; an endless 4s rotate 1turn spin; an endless transform rotate(360deg) spin; an endless 0.5s to-only scale pulse; an endless scale pulse from 1 on .site-aside, with the checklist message; an endless translate pulse from 0; and pulses written from none (individual scale, transform and rotate on the tags, scale on the checklist), 4 of 4 each. Also failed: a steps(2) endless scale from none, a paused endless scale and a scroll-driven scale on the tags. The checklist's pinned inline styles are now saved and restored after each window (lines 184-186, 232-237). The older half is stated honestly for width and padding: an endless 0.5s alternating width animation on the day tag passed all 12 in 4 of 5 runs and failed in 1, the nondeterminism the lab.json notes and the record now name. The wider residual scope is reported as cl7-sme-001.

turns() (lines 149-154) now treats any whole multiple of 360deg as identity. These passed all 12 in 4 of 4 runs each: rotate 1turn on the tags, rotate x -720deg on the tags, and a filled 0.4s spin-in ending at rotate 1turn. The angle regex stops at the unit letter, so deg, rad, grad and turn all parse. Left over, and fail-safe: a zero-axis rotate (0 0 0 45deg), which draws as identity, still fails task 11 (4 of 4) with the message naming rotating. Exact DOMMatrixReadOnly.isIdentity still rejects floating-point residue. Both were optional or alternative parts of the recommendation, and both are contrived.

The notes (line 87) now say the test rejects a non-identity transform, scale, rotate, translate or zoom on the checklist itself or on a tag. They say an identity value counts only when static or the held end of a finished animation, and only none and 1 count while an animation runs. Matches behaviour: static identity values on all five properties on the tags, plus translateX(0), scale 1 1 and rotate z 0deg on the checklist, passed all 12 (4 of 4). An endless opacity-only animation combined with a static translate 0 on the tags failed task 11 (4 of 4), which the 'while an animation is still running' clause covers. The endless-animation sentence was corrected too, but its residual examples are now too narrow (cl7-sme-001).

All three original variants fail task 11 at 80eff5af, 3 of 3 runs each: (a) a forwards-filled animation holding another width on .pack-tag-day fails on the layout-width assertion; (b) an infinite scale animation on both tags fails on the unscaled assertion; (c) a forwards-filled animation holding another padding on .pack-tag-overnight fails on the padding assertion. Animations are no longer forced off: finite ones are finished (line 142) and the rest are read strictly.

Filled entrances that end at identity now pass all 12, 3 or 4 of each: a fade-up ending at translateY(0) on the tags; the same ending at transform none; the same with the translate property ending at 0 0; a fade-up on .site-aside; a scale-in on .site-aside ending at scale 1; and a zoom-in on .site-aside ending at zoom 1. An endless opacity-only animation on the tags also passes. The related, pre-existing ancestor case is unchanged and fail-safe: a 1s no-fill scale entrance on .page still fails task 11 mid-flight with 'something around it is scaling it' (3 of 3), because only the checklist's and tags' own animations are finished. That is cl5-edu-002's scope.
